To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
E6AP acts as a transcriptional coactivator of estrogen receptor in neurons, and this function is lost in AS mouse model.
E6AP is a transcriptional co-activator of estrogen receptor (ER) that regulates the transcription of Cyp26b-1, a retinoic acid degrading enzyme, in a manner that antagonizes retinoic acid signaling.

E6AP, a protein involved in the pathology of Angelman syndrome, is a coactivator for the estrogen receptor, and that this coactivation leads to transcriptional changes in the brain that are associated with the pathology of the syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and functional characterization of novel molecular targets for AS, and the potential development of novel treatment strategies.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathobiology and neurological manifestations of AS.
a novel mechanism of transcriptional crosstalk between E6AP, ER, and retinoic acid signaling pathways that may play a crucial role in neurodevelopment and neurodegenerative diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our findings provide a new mechanistic understanding of the molecular basis of AS, which may lead to the development of new therapeutic interventions for this disorder.
the newly discovered transcriptional coactivation functions of the AS protein E6AP and the estrogen receptor may be involved in the pathobiological mechanisms of AS and ASDs.

the loss of E6AP, a coactivator for estrogen receptor in neurons, leads to a novel antagonistic estrogen-retinoid acid signaling in the brain that is associated with transcriptional deregulation of a gene CYP26B1, which is known to be important for learning and memory processes, and this may contribute to the pathophysiology of AS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of the E6AP protein in the AS brain disrupts an antagonistic estrogen-retinoid signaling crosstalk in neurons.
we have identified and demonstrated a novel transcriptional crosstalk between E6AP and estrogen receptor (ER) in the regulation of a gene involved in learning and cognitive processes, Cyp26B1.
the loss of E6AP function in AS and other ASDs may be due to the loss of the transcriptional coactivator functions of E6Ap and ER.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptional regulation by E6AP and the ER may have a critical role in the pathogenesis of AS.
E6AP is a novel transcriptional coactivator of ER and that this function of E6Ap is important in the pathology of Angelman syndrome.
E6AP is not just a protein ligase but it has other functions, and these other functions may be involved in the development of neurodevelopmental disorders like AS and ASDs.
